Developer internals: databaseUpdate() and the registry tables

K.A. Stam

2026-11-12

Source: vignettes/developer_internals.Rmd
developer_internals.Rmd

This guide explains how beFAIR manages its database internally. It covers the two registry tables that track schema state and ETL script history, and walks through every function called during databaseUpdate(). Read this if you need to understand, debug, or extend the system.

1. The registry tables

beFAIR uses two permanent registry tables to coordinate all database operations. They are created once by databaseInitialize() and are never dropped or truncated by the ETL cycle.

table_codebook

One row per codebook in the package. Tracks the canonical schema definition and is the reference point for version comparisons.

Column SQL type Purpose
codebook_id VARCHAR Relative path key, e.g. study/participant; custom codebooks use custom/study/my_assay
codebook_name VARCHAR Matching database table name, e.g. participant
codebook_version VARCHAR SemVer-style string, e.g. "2.1"
authors VARCHAR Codebook author(s)
created_at VARCHAR ISO-8601 creation date
updated_at VARCHAR ISO-8601 last-modified date
n_parameters INT Number of variables in the codebook
codebook_origin VARCHAR "beFAIR" for built-in package codebooks; the project directory basename (e.g. "MyStudy2024") for custom codebooks

Version semantics. Codebook versions are interpreted as major.minor numeric pairs:

  • Major bump (e.g. 1.x → 2.x): the associated data table is dropped and recreated; all data in that table is lost. Use this only when the schema is incompatible with existing data.
  • Minor bump (e.g. 1.1 → 1.2): only the table_codebook metadata row is updated; the data table and its contents are untouched. Use this for description edits, adding optional fields, or other non-breaking changes. Note that all associated ETL scripts will be queued for a re-run.

table_script

One row per script registered with the system. Tracks what was run, when, and whether the output was valid. This includes some flags for TODO’s and warnings in the ETL script.

Column SQL type Purpose
script_id VARCHAR Relative file path, e.g. studies/CHHIL/scripts/participant.R; for external delivery this is the retrieval script, e.g. analyses/myAnalysis/scripts/retrieve_myAnalysis.R
script_hash VARCHAR MD5 of the script file; change triggers re-run
codebook_name VARCHAR Target table for this script; NA for external retrieval scripts (they load multiple tables)
codebook_version VARCHAR Codebook version at last run; drift triggers re-run (internal scripts only)
authors VARCHAR Author(s) from script metadata
created_at VARCHAR Date first added to the registry
updated_at VARCHAR Date of last successful run
run_time DECIMAL Execution time in seconds
flag_TODO INT Count of #TODO comments found in the script
flag_WARN INT Count of warnings captured during execution

Querying the registry tables 

FAIRgroundConnect("LUCID_FAIRPOINT")
con <- FAIRgroundConnection()

DBI::dbReadTable(con, "table_codebook")
DBI::dbReadTable(con, "table_script")

You can also run these during a live session to inspect state mid-update when debugging.

2. databaseUpdate() — the orchestrator

databaseUpdate() coordinates a complete ETL cycle. Its high-level call sequence is:

databaseUpdate()
├── FAIRgroundConnection()           # resolve default connection
├── setSingleUser()                 # lock DB to exclusive mode (MSSQL only)
├── on.exit:
│   ├── setMultiUser()              # restore multi-user mode
│   └── FAIRgroundDisconnect()       # close connection
├── databasePrepareCodebooks()      # sync codebook schema → DB
├── databasePrepareScripts()        # discover scripts needing (re)run
├── for each script:
│   ├── sqlRemoveEntries()          # delete old rows written by this script
│   ├── sourceScript()              # execute ETL script, get databook
│   ├── [validation gate]           # checks databook$validation$status
│   └── databasePrepareData()       # upload data & update table_script
├── databaseUpdateOverview()        # rebuilds study, experiment and analysis table
└── databaseUpdatePublications()    # rebuild publications table

Single-user lock (MSSQL)

When connecting to a Microsoft SQL Server database, databaseUpdate() calls setSingleUser() immediately after establishing the connection. This acquires an exclusive lock on the database, preventing concurrent writes from other sessions during the ETL cycle. The lock is always released by setMultiUser() in an on.exit() handler — even if the function stops early due to an error.

SQLite connections do not support single-user mode; setSingleUser() and setMultiUser() are no-ops for that backend.

on.exit() cleanup guarantee

The on.exit() block (with add = TRUE) runs unconditionally when databaseUpdate() exits, regardless of whether it completes normally or throws an error. It restores multi-user mode and closes the connection. This means you never need to call FAIRgroundDisconnect() manually after databaseUpdate().

Logging

Pass enable_logging = TRUE to write a JSON log for the entire update cycle:

FAIRgroundConnect("LUCID_FAIRPOINT")
databaseUpdate(enable_logging = TRUE)

Log files are written to logs/files/<timestamp>.json (e.g. logs/files/2024-03-15_09-30-00.json). Each log entry is a JSON object with the severity level, timestamp, message, and any named fields passed by the caller.

To read a log after a run:

library(jsonlite)

log_file <- tail(list.files("logs/files", full.names = TRUE), 1)
logs <- stream_in(file(log_file))

See Section 5 for more detail on the logger setup.

3. Step-by-step breakdown

3.1 databasePrepareCodebooks()

Synchronizes the YAML codebook definitions in the package with table_codebook and the actual data tables in the database.

Steps:

  1. Read current table_codebook from the database.

  2. Migration check: if the codebook_origin column is absent (existing databases pre-v0.65), execute:

    ALTER TABLE table_codebook ADD COLUMN codebook_origin VARCHAR(255);
UPDATE table_codebook SET codebook_origin = 'beFAIR';

  3. Build the expected codebook table from package YAMLs and any custom codebooks in codebooks/ via codebookToTable(). Each row carries a codebook_origin value: "beFAIR" for built-in codebooks, or the project directory basename for custom ones.

  4. Loop over each codebook entry and classify it:

For each codebook (package or custom):
│
├── Not in table_codebook?
│   └── NEW → sqlGenerateTable() + sqlPushTable() into table_codebook
│             (row includes codebook_origin)
│
└── Already in table_codebook:
    ├── major version increased?
    │   └── MAJOR BUMP → DROP TABLE + sqlGenerateTable()
    │                  → DELETE old row + sqlPushTable() new row
    │                  ⚠ All data in this table is lost
    │
    ├── minor version increased?
    │   └── MINOR BUMP → UPDATE table_codebook metadata only
    │                   (version, authors, updated_at, n_parameters)
    │
    └── version unchanged?
        └── No action

All detected changes are logged via the beFAIR logger.

3.2 databasePrepareScripts()

Discovers which scripts need to be (re)run and whether each uses internal or external delivery.

Steps:

  1. Read table_script from the database.
  2. Read table_codebook to get current codebook versions.
  3. Scan studies/*/scripts/, experiments/*/scripts/, and analyses/*/scripts/ for .R files.
  4. Compute the MD5 hash of the script file.
  5. Classify each script:
    • New: path not in table_script → insert a placeholder row. Only inserted if the inferred codebook_name (from the filename) exists in table_codebook; otherwise log an error and skip.
    • Hash changed: file was edited since the last run.
    • Codebook version drifted: table_script.codebook_version is behind table_codebook.codebook_version.
    • Up to date: no action.
  6. Suspended scripts: if a filename starts with _ (e.g. _participant.R), the script is skipped entirely. The function checks whether the corresponding script_id (without the underscore) has existing rows in the database and logs a warning if so. This lets maintainers safely disable a script without losing the audit trail.
  7. Return a data frame of scripts to run with columns script_id, codebook_name, and script_hash, ordered by dependency: id_mapping → studyarm → studydesign → participant → event, then experiments, then analyses.

3.3 Per-script loop

databaseUpdate() iterates over the data frame returned by databasePrepareScripts() and runs the standard four-step ETL flow for each script.

3.3.1 sqlRemoveEntries()

Before re-running a script, its previously uploaded rows are deleted:

DELETE FROM <codebook_name> WHERE script_id = '<script_id>'

This ensures that the re-run starts with a clean slate and there are no duplicate or stale rows from a previous version of the script.

3.3.2 sourceScript()

Executes the ETL script and returns a databook object.

  • The script runs in an isolated environment (new.env()) so it cannot accidentally read or overwrite variables in the calling session.
  • The active DBI connection (con) is injected into this environment as the only external dependency.
  • Before execution, all #TODO comments in the source text are counted (flag_TODO).
  • During execution, R warnings are intercepted and counted (flag_WARN); messages are muffled to suppress pointblank output.
  • Execution time is measured with Sys.time().
  • If the script throws an error, sourceScript() logs it and returns NULL; the main loop skips to the next script.

The databook contract. Every ETL script must produce a named list called databook with these fields:

Field Content
$data A data frame with the rows to upload
$codebook The full codebook list object
$codebook_name Character; target table name
$codebook_version Character; version string
$validation Output of validateDataByCodebook()
$run_time Numeric; execution time in seconds (added by sourceScript())
$flag_TODO Integer; #TODO count (added by sourceScript())
$flag_WARN Integer; warning count (added by sourceScript())

codebookToEntries(cb_name, nrow = N) creates the correctly-typed empty $data skeleton. Scripts should build their data in this frame to guarantee column types match the database schema.

A minimal ETL script skeleton looks like this:

# --- Setup ---
databook <- codebookToEntries("participant", nrow = 100)

# --- Fill data ---
databook$data$source_id   <- raw_data$subject_id
databook$data$study_id    <- "MYST1"
databook$data$age         <- raw_data$age_years
# ...

# --- Validate ---
databook$validation <- validateDataByCodebook(databook)

# --- Clean up (required) ---
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("databook")))

The final rm() call is required. sourceScript() reads databook from the script’s local environment after source() returns; leaving other variables behind does not cause errors but wastes memory.

3.3.3 Validation gate

databaseUpdate() checks databook$validation$status:

  • 1 (pass) → proceed to databasePrepareData()
  • 0 (fail) → log the failure, skip upload, continue with the next script

validateDataByCodebook() uses the pointblank package to apply the validation rules in the codebook YAML to databook$data. It also calls checkSourceIdExist() for any table that has a source_id column (except id_mapping itself), which confirms that every non-reserved source_id value exists in the id_mapping table.

Reserved source_id values — BLANK, STD, NEG_CTRL, POS_CTRL, CTRL, BLANK_STD, SAMPLE_STD — bypass the id_mapping lookup. These represent control and blank samples that do not correspond to real participants.

3.3.4 databasePrepareData()

Transforms the validated data and uploads it to the database, then updates table_script.

For id_mapping scripts:

  1. Call addParticipantIds() to generate a deterministic participant_id for each row. The ID is computed as the first 6 hex characters of the SHA-256 hash of the string "<study_id>_<NNNN>" (4-digit zero-padded participant_nr), yielding a value like "MYST1_a3f9b2".
  2. Add the script_id column.
  3. Upload via sqlPushTable().

For all other tables:

  1. If source_id is present: left-join against the id_mapping table to attach participant_id. Reserved IDs receive their own value as participant_id (e.g. participant_id = "BLANK").
  2. If both event_id and timepoint are present: construct event_id = paste0(participant_id, "_", sprintf("%04d", timepoint)). Reserved IDs get event_id = NA.
  3. Add the script_id column.
  4. Upload via sqlPushTable().

After a successful upload, updateTableScript() updates the table_script row for this script with the current MD5 hash, codebook version, updated_at timestamp, run_time, flag_TODO, and flag_WARN.

3.4 Post-loop: databaseUpdateOverview() and databaseUpdatePublications()

After all scripts have been processed, two aggregate tables are always rebuilt unconditionally — even if no individual scripts were updated:

  • databaseUpdateOverview() rebuilds the study, experiment, and analysis aggregate tables.
  • databaseUpdatePublications() rebuilds the publications table.

Because these always run, they reflect the current state of the database regardless of which scripts ran in this cycle.

4. Supporting SQL helpers

sqlGenerateTable(cb_name)

Reads the codebook YAML for cb_name, builds a CREATE TABLE DDL string from the type_sql fields of each variable, and executes it. DECIMAL columns are always created as DECIMAL(38, 18) to preserve precision.

Example of the generated DDL for a simplified codebook:

CREATE TABLE participant (
  script_id VARCHAR,
  source_id VARCHAR,
  study_id VARCHAR,
  participant_nr INT,
  participant_id VARCHAR,
  age DECIMAL(38, 18),
  sex VARCHAR
);

sqlPushTable(data, table_name, script_id)

Wraps DBI::dbWriteTable(..., append = TRUE). On success, logs the number of rows written. On failure, logs the error message and returns FALSE.

sqlRemoveEntries()

Issues a parameterized DELETE statement for the given codebook_name and script_id. See Section 3.3.1 above.

5. Logging

beFAIR uses the lgr package with a named logger hierarchy. All internal functions obtain the logger via:

lg <- lgr::get_logger("beFAIR")

This creates a child logger under the root lgr logger, allowing the threshold and appenders to be configured independently.

.initLogger() and .disableLogger()

.initLogger() is called by databaseUpdate() when enable_logging = TRUE:

  • Clears any existing appenders on the "beFAIR" logger.
  • Sets the threshold to "info".
  • Adds a lgr::AppenderFile with lgr::LayoutJson that writes to logs/files/<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS>.json.

.disableLogger() removes all appenders (flushing pending writes to disk) and is called in the on.exit() handler at the end of databaseUpdate().

Reading log files 

library(jsonlite)

# Find the most recent log file
log_file <- tail(list.files("logs/files", full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.json$"), 1)

# Stream-parse the JSON log (one object per line)
logs <- jsonlite::stream_in(file(log_file), verbose = FALSE)

# Filter to warnings and errors only
logs[logs$level >= 300, c("timestamp", "level_name", "msg", "script_id")]

Log levels follow the lgr convention: info = 200, warn = 300, error = 400, fatal = 500.
